issues.body: require_one_side_bound is still only a public helper whose documentation tells callers to run it before wire::derive_grants. No changed production boundary invokes it, and the acceptance suite calls the helper directly rather than sending an unseeded controller-authored rule through the real admission path. Thus callers can still pass unseedable .acr text directly to derive_grants, contrary to the operational refusal language in the research update and skill documentation.
issues.fix_hint: Enforce the guard at the single shared boundary before controller-authored rule text reaches derive_grants/evaluation, propagate denial fail-closed, and add an integration test proving an unseeded .acr rule is rejected through that real path while a seeded rule succeeds. Otherwise narrow the claims to static analysis only and explicitly state that operational enforcement remains unresolved.
issues.title: Fail-closed seeding guard remains unenforced on the real .acr path

issues.body: is_var still recognizes only terms beginning with '?', and term_bound therefore treats a label such as '_:x' as a bound constant. In an N3 rule formula, a blank-node label is formula-scoped/existential rather than an externally fixed endpoint, so it cannot conservatively provide the constant-side lookup claimed by the one-side-bound guard. A body such as `{ _:x p:linkedTo ?o } => { ?o p:ok p:v }` can still pass incorrectly.
issues.fix_hint: Treat blank-node labels as unbound formula-scoped terms for seeding analysis, or reject them as unsupported. Add a require_one_side_bound regression test demonstrating that a blank-node-labelled endpoint cannot seed an otherwise unbound atom.
issues.title: Blank-node labels are still incorrectly accepted as constant seeds

verdict.summary: Round 2 is stagnant. Both prior major findings remain in the submitted diff: the new fail-closed guard is still only an optional public helper and is not enforced at the shared controller-authored .acr admission boundary, while blank-node labels are still classified as constants by is_var/term_bound. The tests exercise the helper directly but do not prove denial on the real derive_grants path, and no blank-node-label regression test was added.
